name: Cresp 40mcg Injection(Pfs) 0.4ml
introduction:
Introduction About CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS)

CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) contains Darbepoetin alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage symptomatic anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults and children. In kidney failure, the kidney does not produce enough erythropoietin (a natural hormone) which can often cause anemia.

Before CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) management, your doctor may want you to take blood tests to measure how your anaemia is responding and may adjust your dose to maintain long-term control of your condition. Your blood pressure will also be checked regularly, especially at the beginning of your management.

CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients having high blood pressure which is not being controlled. Before receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS), inform your doctor if you have or ever had high blood pressure which is being controlled with medicines, sickle cell anemia, fits, liver disease, lack of response to medicines used to manage anemia, latex allergy or hepatitis C.

CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) should be used with caution in pregnant women. Patients must not breastfeed while receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS). No data is available regarding CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) use in children (less than 1 month old) with CKD receiving and not receiving dialysis. The safety and efficacy of CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) in children with cancer have not been established so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

The most common side effects of receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) are high blood pressure, allergic reactions, pain around the area injected and rash or redness of the skin. Call your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen.
uses: Associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults and children
With non-myeloid malignancies receiving chemotherapy in adult cancer patients
usesDetails:
Uses Of CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS)

Manages symptomatic anemia

mechanismOfAction:
How CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) Works

CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) increases red blood cell counts by stimulating the bone marrow (soft tissue inside the bones where blood is made) to make more red blood cells.
usageDetails:
How to use CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS)

CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse either under your skin (subcutaneous) or into a vein (intravenous). Your doctor will decide on a proper dose and duration depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. Do not stop receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) unless your doctor advises you to stop.
sideEffects: Pain around the area of injection
Rash or redness of the skin
Bruising and bleeding at the site of injection
Blood clots in a dialysis access

Serious skin rashes like Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (reddish macules or circular patches often with central blisters on the trunk, skin peeling, ulcers of mouth, throat, nose, genitals and eyes and fever or flu-like symptoms)
Severe headache, drowsiness, confusion, eyesight problem, nausea, vomiting or fits (could imply very high blood pressure)
Lack of energy and tiredness (pure red cell aplasia (PRCA)), which means that the body has stopped or reduced the production of red blood cells which causes severe anemia

Common
High blood pressure
Allergic reactions
Stroke
Pain around the area of injection
Rash or redness of the skin
Blood clots

Uncommon

Blood clots in a dialysis access
Rare

Stop receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects:

Serious skin rashes like Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (reddish macules or circular patches often with central blisters on the trunk, skin peeling, ulcers of mouth, throat, nose, genitals and eyes and fever or flu-like symptoms)
Severe headache, drowsiness, confusion, eyesight problem, nausea, vomiting or fits (could imply very high blood pressure)
Lack of energy and tiredness (pure red cell aplasia (PRCA)), which means that the body has stopped or reduced the production of red blood cells which causes severe anemia

warnings.details: CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) should be used with caution in pregnant women. If you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or are planning for a baby, consult your doctor before receiving it.
CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women because it is not known if it is excreted in breast milk. Consult your doctor before receiving it.
CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) should not affect the ability to drive or use machines.

In patients with chronic kidney failure, your doctor will adjust the correct dose and duration of CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) management depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. Consult your doctor before receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS).
CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) should be used with caution in patients with liver disease and hepatitis C. Consult your doctor before receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS).

Before receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you are allergic to Darbepoetin alfa or any of the other ingredients of this medicine or latex (Ex. needle cap on the pre-filled syringe).

CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with high blood pressure which is not being controlled with other medicines. CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) should be used with caution in patients with high blood pressure which is being controlled. Consult your doctor before receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS).

Others

Before receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS), inform your doctor if you have:

Sickle cell anemia
Epileptic fits (seizures)
Convulsions
Lack of response to certain medicines used to manage anemia

Use in pediatrics:

No data is available regarding CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) use in children (less than 1-month-old) with CKD receiving and not receiving dialysis. The safety and efficacy of CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) in children with cancer have not been established so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

Use in geriatrics:

No differences in safety or efficacy have been observed between older and younger patients. Consult your doctor before receiving CRESP 40MCG INJECTION(PFS).

name: TRANOSTAT Injection 5x5ml
introduction:
Introduction About TRANOSTAT INJECTION

TRANOSTAT INJECTION contains Tranexamic Acid which belongs to the group of medicines called Antifibrinolytics. It is used in the management of bleeding in conditions such as heavy menstrual bleeding in women, gastrointestinal bleeding (bleeding in digestive tract, anywhere from the throat to rectum), bleeding due to thrombolytic therapy (medicine that is used to breakdown blood clots) and after having surgeries (such as ear, nose, throat, prostate gland, urinary tract, gynecological, abdominal or heart surgery) in adults and children above one year of age.

TRANOSTAT INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with severe kidney impairment, blood clotting disorder or consumption coagulopathy (condition affecting the blood’s ability to clot and stop the bleeding) or history of seizures (fits). Your doctor may recommend you to take relevant tests to understand your existing condition.

Before receiving TRANOSTAT INJECTION, inform your doctor if you had or have blood in the urine, are at risk of having a blood clot, excessive clotting or bleeding throughout the body (disseminated intravascular coagulation).

TRANOSTAT INJECTION is not recommended for use in the first trimester of pregnancy and in breast-feeding women. It should be used with caution in pregnant women only if clearly advised by the doctor. TRANOSTAT INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients, especially in patients with the evidence of renal failure.

The most common side effects of receiving TRANOSTAT INJECTION are nausea or vomiting and diarrhea. Inform your doctor immediately if any of the side effect worsens.
uses: Heavy menstrual bleeding in women
Gastrointestinal bleeding
After having surgeries (such as ear, nose, throat, heart, abdominal, gynaecological and prostrate or urinary tract surgery)
Bleeding due to medicine that is used to breakdown blood clots (thrombolytic therapy)

Uses Of TRANOSTAT INJECTION

mechanismOfAction:
How TRANOSTAT INJECTION Works

TRANOSTAT INJECTION manages bleeding by blocking the plasminogen from binding with fibrin which results in bleeding. As a result, it manages and controls bleeding associated with various factors.
usageDetails:
How to use TRANOSTAT INJECTION

TRANOSTAT INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into a vein as an intravenous injection. Your doctor will decide the correct dose, frequency and duration for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.
sideEffects: Severe allergic reaction (signs include redness of the skin and lumpy skin rashes, difficulty in breathing, swelling of face, mouth, lips or eyelids, unexplained high temperature (fever) and fainting)
Swelling of the throat that causes breathing and swallowing difficulty
Symptoms of a blood clot (such as swelling or pain in the legs or chest, headache, weakness of the face and limbs on one side of the body)

Severe allergic reaction (signs include redness of the skin and lumpy skin rashes, difficulty in breathing, swelling of face, mouth, lips or eyelids, unexplained high temperature (fever) and fainting)

warnings.details: TRANOSTAT INJECTION is not recommended for use in the first trimester of pregnancy. It should be used with caution in pregnant women only if considered clearly necessary. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during management with this medicine. Consult your doctor before receiving TRANOSTAT INJECTION.
TRANOSTAT INJECTION is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women as it passes through breast milk. Consult your doctor for advice.

TRANOSTAT INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with severe kidney impairment. It should be used with caution in patients with mild to moderate kidney impairment. Your doctor may adjust the dose depending upon the kidney function. Consult your doctor before receiving TRANOSTAT INJECTION.
TRANOSTAT INJECTION can be used with caution in patients with liver impairment. Consult your doctor before receiving TRANOSTAT INJECTION.
Do not receive TRANOSTAT INJECTION if you are allergic to Tranexamic acid or any other ingredients of this medicine.

TRANOSTAT INJECTION should be used with caution in children above 1 year of age. Your child’s doctor will adjust the dose based on the bodyweight of the child. Consult child’s doctor for advice before administration of TRANOSTAT INJECTION.
TRANOSTAT INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients, especially in patients with the evidence of renal failure. Consult your doctor before receiving TRANOSTAT INJECTION.

Others

TRANOSTAT INJECTION is not recommended for use if you:

Have blood clotting disorder or consumption coagulopathy (condition affecting the blood’s ability to clot and stop the bleeding)
Have history of seizures (fits)

Before receiving TRANOSTAT INJECTION, inform your physician if you:

Have blood in the urine (which may lead to urinary tract obstruction)
Are at risk of having a blood clot
Have excessive clotting or bleeding throughout the body (disseminated intravascular coagulation)

name: Anfoe 10000IU Injection 1ml
introduction:
Introduction About ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage or manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION Works

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

Signs of allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of the eyes, face, lips, tongue or throat leading to difficulty in breathing or swallowing)

warnings.details: It is not known whether the use of ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION can harm the growing baby. Therefore, it should be used in pregnant women and in women planning to become pregnant only if considered necessary by the physician.
It is not known whether ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION can pass through breast milk or not. Therefore, it should be used in breastfeeding women only if considered necessary by the physician.
Do not drive or handle any heavy tools or machines if your ability is affected by ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION.
Avoid consumption of alcohol before receiving ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION.
ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION should be used with caution in patients undergoing dialysis. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from liver diseases. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
Talk to your doctor before receiving ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION if you are allergic to Epoetin Alfa.

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with severe heart diseases (including recent heart attack). It should be used with caution in patients with other mild heart problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

Others

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use if you:

Have Pure Red cell aplasia (a condition in which bone marrow cannot produce red blood cells)
Have uncontrollable high blood pressure
Have severe disorders of blood vessels in the body
Had stroke recently
Cannot have blood transfusion with your own blood
Cannot take blood thinning medicines

Before receiving ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have:

Have diabetes
Are obese or overweight
Have a previous history of blood clots in the body
Are bed-ridden for a prolonged period
Have or ever suffered a high blood pressure
Have or ever had epilepsy (fits)
Have anemia of other causes not listed above
Have porphyria (a rare inherited blood disorder)
Have head and neck cancer, breast cancer

Use in paediatrics:

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION should be used in children and in adolescents (aged below 18 years) only if prescribed by the physician. It is not suitable for use in young babies (aged below 1 year). Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before administration.

Use in geriatrics:

ANFOE 10000IU INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

introduction:
Introduction About DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS)

DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) contains Darbepoetin alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage symptomatic anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults and children. In kidney failure, the kidney does not produce enough erythropoietin (a natural hormone) which can often cause anemia.

Before DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) management, your doctor may want you to take blood tests to measure how your anaemia is responding and may adjust your dose to maintain long-term control of your condition. Your blood pressure will also be checked regularly, especially at the beginning of your management.

DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients having high blood pressure which is not being controlled. Before receiving DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS), inform your doctor if you have or ever had high blood pressure which is being controlled with medicines, sickle cell anemia, fits, liver disease, lack of response to medicines used to manage anemia, latex allergy or hepatitis C.

DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) should be used with caution in pregnant women. Patients must not breastfeed while receiving DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS). No data is available regarding DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) use in children (less than 1 month old) with CKD receiving and not receiving dialysis. The safety and efficacy of DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) in children with cancer have not been established so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

The most common side effects of receiving DARGEN 40MCG INJECTION(PFS) are high blood pressure, allergic reactions, pain around the area injected and rash or redness of the skin. Call your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen.

introduction:
Introduction About WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS)

WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) Works

WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS)

WEPOX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION

EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION Works

EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION

EPOCEPT 4000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

How WEPOX 1000IU INJECTION Works

WEPOX 1000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. mechanismOfAction:
How EPORISE 40000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE Works

EPORISE 40000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.

It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

Introduction About ERYPRO SAFE 5000IU INJECTION(PFS)

ERYPRO SAFE 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. Before receiving ERYPRO SAFE 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

ERYPRO SAFE 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving ERYPRO SAFE 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving ERYPRO SAFE 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION

RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About ENCOURAGE 2000IU INJECTION

ENCOURAGE 2000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

ENCOURAGE 2000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with ENCOURAGE 2000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving ENCOURAGE 2000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

ENCOURAGE 2000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving ENCOURAGE 2000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving ENCOURAGE 2000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

name: Dargen 60mcg Prefilled Syringe 1'S
introduction:
Introduction About DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE

DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE contains Darbepoetin alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage symptomatic anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults and children. In kidney failure, the kidney does not produce enough erythropoietin (a natural hormone) which can often cause anemia.

Before DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE management, your doctor may want you to take blood tests to measure how your anaemia is responding and may adjust your dose to maintain long-term control of your condition. Your blood pressure will also be checked regularly, especially at the beginning of your management.

DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE is not recommended for use in patients having high blood pressure which is not being controlled. Before receiving DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE, inform your doctor if you have or ever had high blood pressure which is being controlled with medicines, sickle cell anemia, fits, liver disease, lack of response to medicines used to manage anemia, latex allergy or hepatitis C.

DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE should be used with caution in pregnant women. Patients must not breastfeed while receiving DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE. No data is available regarding DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE use in children (less than 1 month old) with CKD receiving and not receiving dialysis. The safety and efficacy of DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE in children with cancer have not been established so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

The most common side effects of receiving DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE are high blood pressure, allergic reactions, pain around the area injected and rash or redness of the skin. Call your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen.
uses: Associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults and children
With non-myeloid malignancies receiving chemotherapy in adult cancer patients

mechanismOfAction:
How DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE Works

DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE increases red blood cell counts by stimulating the bone marrow (soft tissue inside the bones where blood is made) to make more red blood cells.
usageDetails:
How to use DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE

DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse either under your skin (subcutaneous) or into a vein (intravenous). Your doctor will decide on a proper dose and duration depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. Do not stop receiving DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE unless your doctor advises you to stop.
sideEffects: Pain around the area of injection
Rash or redness of the skin
Bruising and bleeding at the site of injection
Blood clots in a dialysis access

Serious skin rashes like Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (reddish macules or circular patches often with central blisters on the trunk, skin peeling, ulcers of mouth, throat, nose, genitals and eyes and fever or flu-like symptoms)
Severe headache, drowsiness, confusion, eyesight problem, nausea, vomiting or fits (could imply very high blood pressure)
Lack of energy and tiredness (pure red cell aplasia (PRCA)), which means that the body has stopped or reduced the production of red blood cells which causes severe anemia

Common
High blood pressure
Allergic reactions
Stroke
Pain around the area of injection
Rash or redness of the skin

Rare

Stop receiving DARGEN 60MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects:

Serious skin rashes like Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (reddish macules or circular patches often with central blisters on the trunk, skin peeling, ulcers of mouth, throat, nose, genitals and eyes and fever or flu-like symptoms)
Severe headache, drowsiness, confusion, eyesight problem, nausea, vomiting or fits (could imply very high blood pressure)
Lack of energy and tiredness (pure red cell aplasia (PRCA)), which means that the body has stopped or reduced the production of red blood cells which causes severe anemia

introduction:
Introduction About NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION

NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION Works

NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION

NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

Severe skin reactions (such as skin rash, blistering and peeling of the skin and soft tissues, skin rash on the face, legs, genitals, trunk, reddish target-like spots or circular patches often with central blisters on the trunk, ulcers of mouth, throat, nose, genitals and eyes and can be preceded by fever and flu-like symptoms)
Signs of allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of the eyes, face, lips, tongue or throat leading to difficulty in breathing or swallowing)
Uncontrollably severe increase in blood pressure

It is not known whether NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION can pass through breast milk or not. Therefore, it should be used in breastfeeding women only if considered necessary by the physician.
Do not drive or handle any heavy tools or machines if your ability is affected by NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION.
Avoid consumption of alcohol before receiving NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION.
NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION should be used with caution in patients undergoing dialysis. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION should be used with caution in patients suffering from liver diseases. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
Talk to your doctor before receiving NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION if you are allergic to Epoetin Alfa.

NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with severe heart diseases (including recent heart attack). It should be used with caution in patients with other mild heart problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION should be used in children and in adolescents (aged below 18 years) only if prescribed by the physician. It is not suitable for use in young babies (aged below 1 year). Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before administration.
NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

Others

NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use if you:

Have Pure Red cell aplasia (a condition in which bone marrow cannot produce red blood cells)
Have uncontrollable high blood pressure
Have severe disorders of blood vessels in the body
Had stroke recently
Cannot have blood transfusion with your own blood
Cannot take blood thinning medicines

Before receiving NEO RECORMON 5000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have:

Have diabetes
Are obese or overweight
Have a previous history of blood clots in the body
Are bed-ridden for a prolonged period
Have or ever suffered a high blood pressure
Have or ever had epilepsy (fits)
Have anemia of other causes not listed above
Have porphyria (a rare inherited blood disorder)
Have head and neck cancer, breast cancer

WEPOX SAFE 5000 INJECTION(PFS) is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with WEPOX SAFE 5000 INJECTION(PFS) your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving WEPOX SAFE 5000 INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

mechanismOfAction:
How WEPOX SAFE 5000 INJECTION(PFS) Works

WEPOX SAFE 5000 INJECTION(PFS) is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.

WEPOX SAFE 5000 INJECTION(PFS) will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

Introduction About EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION

EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

How EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION Works

EPORISE 40000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.

introduction:
Introduction About EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION

EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION Works

EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION

EPOTRUST 3000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS)

BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS) contains Darbepoetin alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage symptomatic anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults and children. In kidney failure, the kidney does not produce enough erythropoietin (a natural hormone) which can often cause anemia.

Before BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS) management, your doctor may want you to take blood tests to measure how your anaemia is responding and may adjust your dose to maintain long-term control of your condition. Your blood pressure will also be checked regularly, especially at the beginning of your management.

BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients having high blood pressure which is not being controlled. Before receiving BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS), inform your doctor if you have or ever had high blood pressure which is being controlled with medicines, sickle cell anemia, fits, liver disease, lack of response to medicines used to manage anemia, latex allergy or hepatitis C.

BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS) should be used with caution in pregnant women. Patients must not breastfeed while receiving BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS). No data is available regarding BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS) use in children (less than 1 month old) with CKD receiving and not receiving dialysis. The safety and efficacy of BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS) in children with cancer have not been established so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

The most common side effects of receiving BIONESP 25MCG INJECTION(PFS) are high blood pressure, allergic reactions, pain around the area injected and rash or redness of the skin. Call your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen.

Anemia (low RBC in blood) caused due to chronic kidney disease, chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes),

mechanismOfAction:
How SHANPOIETIN 5000IU INJECTION Works

SHANPOIETIN 5000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.

SHANPOIETIN 5000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About RPO 3000IU INJECTION(PFS)

RPO 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

RPO 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with RPO 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving RPO 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

RPO 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving RPO 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving RPO 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

name: TRANTAS Injection 5ml
introduction:
Introduction About TRANTAS INJECTION

TRANTAS INJECTION contains Tranexamic Acid which belongs to the group of medicines called Antifibrinolytics. It is used in the management of bleeding in conditions such as heavy menstrual bleeding in women, gastrointestinal bleeding (bleeding in digestive tract, anywhere from the throat to rectum), bleeding due to thrombolytic therapy (medicine that is used to breakdown blood clots) and after having surgeries (such as ear, nose, throat, prostate gland, urinary tract, gynecological, abdominal or heart surgery) in adults and children above one year of age.

TRANTAS INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with severe kidney impairment, blood clotting disorder or consumption coagulopathy (condition affecting the blood’s ability to clot and stop the bleeding) or history of seizures (fits). Your doctor may recommend you to take relevant tests to understand your existing condition.

Before receiving TRANTAS INJECTION, inform your doctor if you had or have blood in the urine, are at risk of having a blood clot, excessive clotting or bleeding throughout the body (disseminated intravascular coagulation).

TRANTAS INJECTION is not recommended for use in the first trimester of pregnancy and in breast-feeding women. It should be used with caution in pregnant women only if clearly advised by the doctor. TRANTAS INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients, especially in patients with the evidence of renal failure.

The most common side effects of receiving TRANTAS INJECTION are nausea or vomiting and diarrhea. Inform your doctor immediately if any of the side effect worsens.

introduction:
Introduction About EPOTRUST 5000IU INJECTION(PFS)

EPOTRUST 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPOTRUST 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPOTRUST 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPOTRUST 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPOTRUST 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPOTRUST 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPOTRUST 5000IU INJECTION(PFS) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

introduction:
Introduction About EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS)

EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) Works

EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS)

EPREX 3000IU INJECTION(PFS) will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

Introduction About ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION

ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION Works

ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION

ZYROP 2000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

mechanismOfAction:
How RELIPOIETIN 10000IU INJECTION Works

RELIPOIETIN 10000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.

RELIPOIETIN 10000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). introduction:
Introduction About EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION

EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION Works

EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION

EPOTREND 2000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

Introduction About EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE Works

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

Signs of allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of the eyes, face, lips, tongue or throat leading to difficulty in breathing or swallowing)

Side Effects Of EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE
Common
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting
Fever, chills, flu-like symptoms
Stuffy nose, sore throat, cough
Signs of high blood pressure (such as severe headaches, confusion and fits)
Signs of blood clots in the body (such as chest pain, breathlessness, pain and tenderness of legs)

Feeling weak, tired or dizzy
Swollen legs, ankles or feet

Fits

Severe skin reactions (such as skin rash, blistering and peeling of the skin and soft tissues, skin rash on the face, legs, genitals, trunk, reddish target-like spots or circular patches often with central blisters on the trunk, ulcers of mouth, throat, nose, genitals and eyes and can be preceded by fever and flu-like symptoms)
Signs of allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of the eyes, face, lips, tongue or throat leading to difficulty in breathing or swallowing)
Fits (seizures)
Uncontrollably severe increase in blood pressure

warnings.details: It is not known whether the use of EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE can harm the growing baby. Therefore, it should be used in pregnant women and in women planning to become pregnant only if considered necessary by the physician.
It is not known whether EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE can pass through breast milk or not. Therefore, it should be used in breastfeeding women only if considered necessary by the physician.
Do not drive or handle any heavy tools or machines if your ability is affected by EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE.
Avoid consumption of alcohol before receiving EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE.
EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE should be used with caution in patients undergoing dialysis. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE should be used with caution in patients suffering from liver diseases. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
Talk to your doctor before receiving EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE if you are allergic to Epoetin Alfa.

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE is not recommended for use in patients with severe heart diseases (including recent heart attack). It should be used with caution in patients with other mild heart problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE should be used in children and in adolescents (aged below 18 years) only if prescribed by the physician. It is not suitable for use in young babies (aged below 1 year). Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before administration.
EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE should be used with caution in elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

Others

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE is not recommended for use if you:

Have Pure Red cell aplasia (a condition in which bone marrow cannot produce red blood cells)
Have uncontrollable high blood pressure
Have severe disorders of blood vessels in the body
Had stroke recently
Cannot have blood transfusion with your own blood
Cannot take blood thinning medicines

Before receiving EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE inform your doctor if you have:

Have diabetes
Are obese or overweight
Have a previous history of blood clots in the body
Are bed-ridden for a prolonged period
Have or ever suffered a high blood pressure
Have or ever had epilepsy (fits)
Have anemia of other causes not listed above
Have porphyria (a rare inherited blood disorder)
Have head and neck cancer, breast cancer

Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before receiving EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines such as:

Cyclosporin (a medicine used for immunosuppression in organ transplant patients)
Iron supplements (medicines used for managing iron deficiency anaemia)
Other blood stimulants (medicines used to stimulate blood cell production) Ex. darbepoetin alfa
Interferons (medicines used to manage cancer) Ex. interferon alfa 2A
Ribavirin (a medicine used to manage hepatitis C infection)

Overdosage:

EPORISE 20000IU PREFILLED SYRINGE will be administered to you only by a doctor or a nurse in a hospital and so it is unlikely to receive an overdose. However, consult your doctor or nurse if you experience any unusual symptoms. Symptoms of overdose might include fits and high blood pressure.

introduction:
Introduction About WEPOX 2000IU INJECTION(PFS)

WEPOX 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

WEPOX 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with WEPOX 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving WEPOX 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

WEPOX 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving WEPOX 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving WEPOX 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

introduction:
Introduction About ALPHARED 2000IU INJECTION

ALPHARED 2000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

ALPHARED 2000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with ALPHARED 2000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving ALPHARED 2000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

ALPHARED 2000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving ALPHARED 2000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving ALPHARED 2000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

introduction:
Introduction About ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS)

ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.
