mechanismOfAction:
How ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) Works

ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS)

ERYPRO PREFIL 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION

EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION Works

EPOSIS 1000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.

It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS)

TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) Works

TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.

How to use TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS)

TRANSFER 2000IU INJECTION(PFS) will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About CRESP 25MCG INJECTION

CRESP 25MCG INJECTION contains Darbepoetin alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage symptomatic anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults and children. In kidney failure, the kidney does not produce enough erythropoietin (a natural hormone) which can often cause anemia.

Before CRESP 25MCG INJECTION management, your doctor may want you to take blood tests to measure how your anaemia is responding and may adjust your dose to maintain long-term control of your condition. Your blood pressure will also be checked regularly, especially at the beginning of your management.

CRESP 25MCG INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients having high blood pressure which is not being controlled. Before receiving CRESP 25MCG INJECTION, inform your doctor if you have or ever had high blood pressure which is being controlled with medicines, sickle cell anemia, fits, liver disease, lack of response to medicines used to manage anemia, latex allergy or hepatitis C.

CRESP 25MCG INJECTION should be used with caution in pregnant women. Patients must not breastfeed while receiving CRESP 25MCG INJECTION. No data is available regarding CRESP 25MCG INJECTION use in children (less than 1 month old) with CKD receiving and not receiving dialysis. The safety and efficacy of CRESP 25MCG INJECTION in children with cancer have not been established so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

The most common side effects of receiving CRESP 25MCG INJECTION are high blood pressure, allergic reactions, pain around the area injected and rash or redness of the skin. Call your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen.

introduction:
Introduction About EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION

EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION contains Epoetin Alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage anemia caused due to chronic kidney disease (CKD), chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy (Ex. zidovudine), blood donation or due to any bone marrow disorders/cancers (such as myelodysplastic syndromes).

It can also be used to manage anemia in patients who are planning to undergo any major bone surgery (such as hip or knee replacement operations). It may also reduce the potential need for blood transfusion in cancer patients and in patients undergoing bone surgery or chemotherapy.

EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION is suitable for use both in adults and in children. During management with EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION your doctor will constantly monitor your blood pressure and iron levels in blood and will adjust the dose accordingly to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before receiving EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, fits, previous history of blood clots or if you are undergoing dialysis or any surgery as a precaution.

EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with recent heart attack or stroke. It is also not suitable for use in patients having severe uncontrollable high blood pressure and pure red aplastic anemia (a condition in which the bone marrow cannot produce RBC).

Inform your doctor before receiving EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution. The most common side effects of receiving EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fever, stuffy nose and sore throat. Contact your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

mechanismOfAction:
How EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION Works

EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION is an Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent. Following administration, it stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. It contains a medicine called Epoetin Alfa which acts similar to the endogenous human protein called erythropoietin (a substance that stimulates bone marrow to produce red blood cells).

Therefore, it replaces the lost red blood cells (RBC) in the body of anaemic patients and in patients who are at risk of developing anemia due to chemotherapy, anti-viral therapy or bone marrow disorders.
usageDetails:
How to use EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION

EPOTOP 2000IU INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously) or under the skin (subcutaneously). It can also be self-administered by the patient if instructed by the doctor. Carefully follow the instructions given by your doctor in case of self-administration.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS)

CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) contains Darbepoetin alfa which belongs to the group of medicines called Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. It is used to manage symptomatic anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults and children. In kidney failure, the kidney does not produce enough erythropoietin (a natural hormone) which can often cause anemia.

Before CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) management, your doctor may want you to take blood tests to measure how your anaemia is responding and may adjust your dose to maintain long-term control of your condition. Your blood pressure will also be checked regularly, especially at the beginning of your management.

CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients having high blood pressure which is not being controlled. Before receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS), inform your doctor if you have or ever had high blood pressure which is being controlled with medicines, sickle cell anemia, fits, liver disease, lack of response to medicines used to manage anemia, latex allergy or hepatitis C.

CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) should be used with caution in pregnant women. Patients must not breastfeed while receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS). No data is available regarding CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) use in children (less than 1 month old) with CKD receiving and not receiving dialysis. The safety and efficacy of CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) in children with cancer have not been established so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

The most common side effects of receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) are high blood pressure, allergic reactions, pain around the area injected and rash or redness of the skin. Call your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen.

How CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) Works

CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) increases red blood cell counts by stimulating the bone marrow (soft tissue inside the bones where blood is made) to make more red blood cells.
usageDetails:
How to use CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS)

CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse either under your skin (subcutaneous) or into a vein (intravenous). Your doctor will decide on a proper dose and duration depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. Do not stop receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) unless your doctor advises you to stop.

Serious skin rashes like Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (reddish macules or circular patches often with central blisters on the trunk, skin peeling, ulcers of mouth, throat, nose, genitals and eyes and fever or flu-like symptoms)

warnings.details: CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) should be used with caution in pregnant women. If you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or are planning for a baby, consult your doctor before receiving it.
CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women because it is not known if it is excreted in breast milk. Consult your doctor before receiving it.
CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) should not affect the ability to drive or use machines.

In patients with chronic kidney failure, your doctor will adjust the correct dose and duration of CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) management depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. Consult your doctor before receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS).
CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) should be used with caution in patients with liver disease and hepatitis C. Consult your doctor before receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS).

Before receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) inform your doctor if you are allergic to Darbepoetin alfa or any of the other ingredients of this medicine or latex (Ex. needle cap on the pre-filled syringe).

CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) is not recommended for use in patients with high blood pressure which is not being controlled with other medicines. CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) should be used with caution in patients with high blood pressure which is being controlled. Consult your doctor before receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS).

Others

Before receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS), inform your doctor if you have:

Sickle cell anemia
Epileptic fits (seizures)
Convulsions
Lack of response to certain medicines used to manage anemia

Use in pediatrics:

No data is available regarding CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) use in children (less than 1-month-old) with CKD receiving and not receiving dialysis. The safety and efficacy of CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS) in children with cancer have not been established so, consult your child’s doctor for advice.

Use in geriatrics:

No differences in safety or efficacy have been observed between older and younger patients. Consult your doctor before receiving CRESP 200MCG PREFILLED SYRINGE(PFS).
